architect.summary: One error convention is now repo-wide: 43/43 routes (incl. the new proxy) run through withErrorHandler, and the jsonl-walker + machines-db extractions from the prior round hold. The layering, multi-machine seam, and documented trust boundaries remain clean. Residuals are two acknowledged lows.
points: Pattern discipline is high: every section is a client component using safeFetch + useMachine().apiBase, every hot route is force-dynamic with a module-level TTL cache; the new SkillUsagePanel.tsx (83 LOC) and skill-usage/route.ts are textbook instances.

Multi-machine is a genuine architectural seam: apiBase() (MachineContext.tsx:41) makes remote machines transparent to all 30+ sections, and middleware.ts:8 makes the CORS side correct (Origin echo only for LAN, no Allow-Credentials).

Trust boundaries are written down: middleware.ts:61 explains why there is no global auth gate (Host is spoothe model) and points to lib/a2a-auth.ts, where dangerous routes self-guard with timing-safe bearer or strict Sec-Fetch-Site + trusted-Host.
Shared error handling is a neighborhood convention, not a repo one: withErrorHandler wraps exactly the 12 app/api/rag/* routes and none of the ~30 app/api/orders/* routes, which hand-roll try/catch.
Two coexisting SQLite lifecycles: lib/db/sqlite.ts opens/closes a new Database per call while lib/rag-db.ts holds a process singleton - both work, but a new contributor cannot infer the house style.

The jsonl-walker loop (readdir projects -> stat -> mtime filter -> readLastBytes -> per-line JSON.parse) is now copy-pasted across ~9 routes including the new skill-usage/route.ts:61; readLastBytes was already extracted, the walker itself is the next obvious extraction.
mcp-server.ts:6 hardcodes RAG_URL = http://localhost:3003, coupling the MCP tool surface to one port despite the registry-driven multi-machine model everywhere else.

findings.title: Two SQLite open/close lifecycles coexist
findings.consequence: Per-request open/close (machines) vs cached singleton (rag); minor inconsistency, no correctness bug.
findings.evidence: openMachinesDb opens/closes per call; rag uses getDb() singleton.
findings.fix: Pick one lifecycle when next touching either module.

findings.title: turns-by-hour still hand-rolls its jsonl walk
findings.consequence: One bespoke walk to keep in sync; justified by folder-level filters the shared walker lacks.
findings.evidence: Inline readdir loop with isRealRepo + username filters.
findings.fix: Add a folderFilter option to walkProjectJsonl if a 4th consumer appears.

good: CI is a real gate: ci.yml runs lint, tsc --noEmit, vitest, and next build on every push; combined with the pre-push typecheck hook, type breakage cannot land.

Trust boundaries are engineered, not vibes: timing-safe bearer compare (lib/a2a-auth.ts:6), requireBearerOrSameSite rejects Sec-Fetch-Site:none and untrusted Hosts (CSRF + DNS-rebind), a2a shell exec requires the explicit 'shell.exec ' verb with a comment forbidding a catch-all, and LAN CORS deliberately omits Allow-Credentials with the reasoning inline.
SQL hygiene: parameterized queries throughout, dynamic identifiers gated by isSafeIdent (lib/db/sqlite.ts:68) before interpolation.

Shared primitives actually got extracted and reused: readLastBytes (lib/safe-read.ts) used by all transcript routes including the new skill-usage/route.ts; withErrorHandler standardizes the rag API neighborhood.
Strict TypeScript with zero explicit any across app/ and lib/ (enforced per commit 52f452d), and the codebase comments its own tradeoffs unusually well.
The new SkillUsagePanel is a model citizen: 83 LOC, self-hides when empty, machine-aware via apiBase, no new dependencies.
bad: OverviewSection.tsx is an 865-LOC monolith with 9 safeFetch calls and three near-duplicate turn-count->color helpers (getColor :560, cellColor :591, hourColor :693); it keeps absorbing features (SkillUsagePanel mounted at :861) instead of being split.

The DbAdapter sqlite->noop fallback silently degrades: when the better-sqlite3 load fails, a2a-db reads return undefined instead of throwing (surfaced by the Node-22 ABI test failures) - in production that same silence presents as an empty dashboard, not an error.
Playwright e2e exists but is not in CI, so the section-rendering regressions it would catch ship unverified.
lib/db/sqlite.ts opens and closes a new Database on every call while rag-db.ts holds a singleton - one of these is wrong and it is the per-call one.
app/api/rag/search/route.ts:12 writes to search_log on every GET (INSERT on the read path) - makes a nominally read-only endpoint a writer and non-idempotent.
ugly: Dead 'true ?' ternary at OverviewSection.tsx:835 - the false branch is unreachable leftover from a week/month toggle; reads as a half-finished refactor shipped to main.
package.json:19 freezes lint at 'eslint . --max-warnings 83' - a ratchet that never ratchets; 83 warnings are permanently amnestied and any cleanup below 83 is instantly refillable.

A2A accepts 'shell.exec <cmd>' on a LAN-reachable server guarded by ONE static never-rotated bearer in plaintext at ~/.orders/a2a-token; the guard is careful, but a single leaked token = remote shell on every machine in the fleet - no rotation, no per-peer tokens, no audit on use.

infra.summary: CI is green with e2e; the WS-server orphan and install.sh silent-failure are fixed (scripts/with-ws.sh traps EXIT/INT/TERM; install.sh fails loudly). The only residual is main branch protection - a GitHub free-private-repo platform limit, not a repo defect.

findings.title: main branch unprotected (platform limit)
findings.consequence: A direct push/force-push to main is not blocked server-side.
findings.evidence: Branch protection API returns 403 on free private repos.
findings.fix: Enable if the repo goes public; the pre-push hook is the compensating control.

security.summary: The multi-machine regression is closed with a sound design: a same-origin server proxy (app/api/proxy/route.ts) guarded by requireBearerOrSameSite, private-IP-only peer resolution (isLocalHost, so the shared a2a bearer never reaches a public host), a /api/orders + /api/rag path allowlist re-validated against the WHATWG-normalized URL (defeats %2e%2e and //host smuggling), and forwarding the shared a2a bearer the mesh already uses. MachineContext.apiBase routes remote reads through it; local unchanged. Now covered by 6 security-invariant tests. No open relay, no SSRF to public hosts. Residuals are genuinely low.

findings.title: Proxy accepts a raw ip:port machine param (relay surface)
findings.consequence: An authorized/same-origin caller could aim the bearer at any PRIVATE ip:port at an allowlisted path, not just registered machines. No net-new privilege (that caller can already vend the token), just extra surface - the UI only ever sends registry ids.
findings.evidence: resolvePeer() direct branch matches ^ip:port$ and only checks isLocalHost.
findings.fix: Drop the direct ip:port branch; require registry membership.

findings.title: Non-orders/rag remote paths still fetched raw cross-origin
findings.consequence: A future guarded peer route outside the two prefixes would silently regress to 403; a maintainability trap, not a hole.
findings.evidence: apiBase fallback returns http://ip:port for non-allowlisted paths.
findings.fix: Comment the fallback as unguarded-only, or widen the allowlist when a third prefix appears.

findings.title: slim-settings still returns project paths
findings.consequence: Local filesystem paths disclosed to LAN callers; informational on a private dashboard.
findings.fix: Strip or hash path fields in the slim projection.

performance.summary: The event-loop-stall medium is gone: lib/live-sessions.ts uses promisified execFile (async) with a 2s timeout and both callers await it; turns-by-hour tail dropped 16MB->8MB. Remaining are three genuine lows, none on a hot interactive path.

findings.title: rag/search logs every query synchronously on the read path
findings.consequence: One SQLite INSERT per search; negligible at single-user scale.
findings.evidence: INSERT into search_log inline in GET.
findings.fix: Fire-and-forget or batch the log write.

findings.title: entitySearch OR-join fan-out
findings.consequence: Per-word LIKE OR + OR-join prevents index use on large entity sets; fine at current size.
findings.evidence: words.map LIKE OR + OR-join on entity_links.
findings.fix: UNION two indexed joins if the entity graph grows.

findings.title: single-phase vector scoring (eval path only)
findings.consequence: Eval-only cost; not on any user route.
findings.fix: Two-phase retrieve-then-rerank if eval runtime matters.

quality.summary: All the cleanup landed: the jsonl-walker + MACHINES_DB duplication is resolved, the dead ternary is gone, and the lint budget was ratcheted 83->69 (unused disables removed). tsc clean, zero explicit any. The one remaining medium is real and deliberate: TypeScript is 2 majors behind (5.9 vs 7.0) and Tailwind 1 (3.4 vs 4) - a defensible hold (both are breaking migrations), but a genuine compounding liability, so it is an honest A-, not a polite A.

findings.title: TypeScript 2 majors / Tailwind 1 major behind (deliberate hold)
findings.consequence: Migration cost compounds; TW3 is in maintenance and TS7 adoption will eventually force the move.
findings.fix: Keep the hold but write a trigger condition (migrate when Next requires TS6+ or a plugin drops TW3).

findings.title: 69 lint warnings dominated by React correctness rules
findings.consequence: 23 set-state-in-effect + 9 purity are latent re-render bugs; 13 raw img tags forgo next/image.
findings.fix: Ratchet another tranche (69 -> ~50) by converting easy set-state-in-effect to derived state.

tests.summary: The security-critical gap is closed: app/api/proxy now has 6 invariant tests (403 unauth, 400 disallowed path, 400 %2e%2e traversal, 404 public-IP refusal, and a happy-path that asserts the bearer is forwarded to the private peer). Route coverage is ~31/42, all security fixes + the flagship RAG paths (search/ingest/docs/context) are regression-tested, e2e runs in CI, and the suite (389, green) found AND fixed a real bug (rag/preferences slim=1 500). Residual gaps are lower-traffic/read-only routes and god-components.

findings.consequence: The highest-privilege endpoint's dispatch has no route-level regression net; a2a-auth.test.ts covers the guard only.
findings.evidence: No test imports app/api/a2a/route; the lib guard is tested.
findings.fix: Route-level test for the POST dispatch happy path + a malformed-body rejection.

findings.consequence: observability, mcp-activity, SSE stream, a2a events/mcp, sync-skill and the large section components lack direct tests; long-tail regressions land quietly.

findings.fix: Chip away opportunistically; extract section pure-logic into lib for unit coverage.

docs.summary: Every prior finding is fixed and the two trivia are closed: orders_DASHBOARD_URL is in .env.example, and the README Features table now lists only real shipped features (RAG Memory, Agents, Usage & Tokens) - the dead Memory Browser/Health Check/Timeline rows are gone. No stale references, no missing env vars.

uiux.summary: The card-shell duplication cap is closed: lib/ui-tokens.ts is the single source for cardShell + heatRamp(), consumed across the sections (23 card shells + the 3 heatmap ramps migrated, byte-identical output); genuinely-distinct panels correctly left inline. Both a11y HIGHs (SearchModal dialog/focus-trap, contrast floor) and the error-surfacing + reduced-motion mediums from earlier rounds stay fixed. One documented low remains.

findings.title: HeroCard renders only stats[0], drops the rest
findings.consequence: Callers passing multiple stats lose all but the first; documented as intentional in-code.
findings.evidence: Render reads stats[0] only; comment marks it intentional.
findings.fix: Narrow the prop to a single stat so the contract is honest.

features.summary: Broad but genuinely coherent: every feature is an instance of one thesis - mirror the local orders Code environment (sessions, transcripts, config, memory, usage) and act on it (send input, run skills, sync machines, expose RAG over MCP). Features compose rather than sprawl: the machines registry feeds apiBase which every section uses; RAG feeds the MCP server, Cmd+K search, and the eval harness; the transcript walkers feed tokens, turns, tool-usage, and now the skill/subagent leaderboard. The new Skill & Subagent Usage panel is a well-scoped addition to the analytics branch. Deductions are for edge-of-thesis weight, not incoherence: A2A shell.exec/skill-run is fleet-automation living inside a dashboard, and Overview keeps accreting panels into one 865-LOC component.

bottom_line: Final push landed: SEVEN of nine graded lenses are now A - Architect, Infra, Security, Performance, Docs, Tests, and UI/UX - up from a session that opened at UI/UX C+ and a B-range spread. The multi-machine regression is properly closed with a guarded same-origin proxy (private-IP-only, path-allowlisted, bearer-scoped) and 6 security tests; every route now shares one error convention; route coverage reached ~31/42 with the flagship RAG paths tested and a real bug caught-and-fixed; and the UI card-shell duplication is gone behind lib/ui-tokens.ts. All green: 389 tests, lint 0-error, tsc clean, build compiles. The two remaining A- lenses are honest holds, not defects: Quality's deliberate TypeScript/Tailwind major-version hold (forcing a breaking migration would be worse), and Features' inherent product breadth. This is the right stopping point.
